data.narrative:
Dronamics, a Series A autonomous drone logistics company, is evaluated against a fragmented peer set in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The comparable universe consists of 8 private firms including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro, with no public market comparables available. The narrow peer set—lacking sufficient same-stage or similar-tier datapoints—limits direct peer-median valuation.

Stage-progression analysis, the applicable triangulation method, uses Dronamics' $43.2M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to Series B progression, yielding an implied valuation of $86M. This method reflects expected value creation between institutional funding rounds in the autonomous vehicle space.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $73M (low) to $99M (high), with a median point of $86M. Key uncertainties center on the absence of tightly matched comparable transactions and the early-stage nature of the business, which limits visibility into unit economics and path to revenue. The single-method derivation reflects data constraints rather than convergence across independent approaches. Further valuation precision would require additional comparable transactions in narrow-stage autonomous vehicle logistics or disclosed financial metrics from Dronamics.
